title: Sex Proportions Across Penguin Species
text:
Are the proportions of male and female penguins similar across different species? I use R to compare the sex proportion across Adelie, Chinstrap, and Gentoo penguins.
Data source: Palmer Penguins, collected and made available by Dr. Kristen Gorman and Palmer Station Antarctica LTER. The data are available under the CC0 license. I access the data through the R palmerpenguins package.
Original study: Gorman, K. B., Williams, T. D., and Fraser, W. R. (2014). Ecological sexual dimorphism and environmental variability within a community of Antarctic penguins (genus Pygoscelis). PLOS ONE, 9(3), e90081.

Clean the data
I keep records with non-missing species and sex. Missing values in other columns will not affect this analysis.

penguin_data <- penguin_data %>%
  drop_na(species, sex) %>%
  select(species, sex)

title: Sex Proportions Across Penguin Species
text:
Calculate sex proportions
I count female and male penguins within each species, then calculate percentages using the number of penguins with recorded sex in that species as the denominator.

sex_summary <- penguin_data %>%
  group_by(species) %>%
  count(sex) %>%
  mutate(percent = round(n / sum(n) * 100,1)) %>%
  ungroup()

sex_summary

# A tibble: 6 × 4
  species   sex        n percent
  <fct>     <fct>  <int>   <dbl>
1 Adelie    female    73    50  
2 Adelie    male      73    50  
3 Chinstrap female    34    50  
4 Chinstrap male      34    50  
5 Gentoo    female    58    48.7
6 Gentoo    male      61    51.3

title: Sex Proportions Across Penguin Species
text:
Compare sex proportions visually
Each species has two bars showing the percentages of female and male penguins with recorded sex.

ggplot(sex_summary, aes(x = species, y = percent, fill = sex)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  labs(x = "Species", y = "Percentage (%)", fill = "Sex")







Figure 1: Female and male percentages within each penguin species, excluding records with missing species or sex.

title: Sex Proportions Across Penguin Species
text:
Conclusion
The proportions of female and male penguins are similar across the three species in this sample. Adelie and Chinstrap penguins have equal proportions of females and males, while Gentoo penguins have a slightly higher proportion of males.
These results include only penguins with recorded species and sex. They describe the observed sample and do not necessarily represent the sex proportions of the entire penguin populations.

title: My first weeks in MDS
text:
The first week on campus.


My first two weeks in the MDS program have been exciting and also a little stressful. During orientation, I was really happy to meet many new classmates and learn more about the program. We also learned about the graduation requirements and the course structure. After hearing about all the courses and requirements, I realized that the program would be very intensive, which made me feel a little nervous about the coming months.
During our first week of classes, most other programs at UBC had not started yet, so there were not many people on campus. However, we quickly became busy with our courses. We have four labs and several worksheets every week, so there is always something to work on. Even though every day is busy, I also feel that my time is very fulfilling.
So far, I have learned a lot of practical knowledge and useful skills in a very short time. The workload is heavier and the pace is faster than I expected, but I am gradually getting used to it. I hope that I can continue learning new things, improve my data science skills, and enjoy the rest of my time in the MDS program.

title: Comparing Body Mass Across Penguin Species
text:
Clean the data
For this comparison, I need species and body mass. I remove rows with missing values in either column, while keeping rows that have missing values in unrelated columns.

mass_data = penguins.dropna(subset=["species", "body_mass_g"]).copy()

print("Original rows:", len(penguins))
print("Rows kept:", len(mass_data))
print("Rows removed:", len(penguins) - len(mass_data))

Original rows: 344
Rows kept: 342
Rows removed: 2

title: Comparing Body Mass Across Penguin Species
text:
Summarize body mass by species
I calculate the sample size, mean, and median body mass for each species. Body mass is measured in grams.

mass_summary = (
    mass_data.groupby("species")
    .agg(
        sample_size=("body_mass_g", "count"),
        mean_mass_g=("body_mass_g", "mean"),
        median_mass_g=("body_mass_g", "median")
    )
    .round(1)
)

title: Comparing Body Mass Across Penguin Species
text:
Compare body mass distributions
The boxplots show the median and spread of body mass within each species.

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

mass_data.boxplot(column="body_mass_g", by="species")
plt.suptitle("")
plt.title("Body mass by penguin species")
plt.xlabel("Species")
plt.ylabel("Body mass (g)")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()







Figure 1: Body mass distributions by penguin species, excluding records with missing species or body mass.

title: Comparing Body Mass Across Penguin Species
text:
Conclusion
Among the 342 penguins with non-missing species and body mass, Gentoo penguins have the highest mean body mass (5,076.0 g). Adelie and Chinstrap penguins have similar mean body masses of 3,700.7 g and 3,733.1 g, respectively.
These results describe the penguins in this dataset. The boxplots also show variation in body mass within each species. This analysis also does not account for sex or other factors that may be associated with body mass.
